I farm for a living, so I would keep my plan steady and labor-saving. I am 63, my family has off-farm work, and I have only 30 mu, so I would not spread myself too thin with too many changes. My main land would still stay in the wheat-maize system because I know it well, the yield is steady, and I have well irrigation, so I can protect production in dry periods. I would keep smaller areas in cotton and garlic because they bring cash, but I would not expand them too much since they need more field watching and more pest control. I would use better seed where it helps yield and stability, put more fertilizer on wheat and maize because they are my backbone crops, keep irrigation focused on key stages, and use simpler tillage where I can save labor, especially for maize after wheat. My goal would be stable output first, then cash income, not taking big risks.
